subject.title: [Security] Mitigating timing attacks in GitHub Auth OAuth callback validation

question: Should the security team close this report as no-action because current GitHub Copilot authentication has no callback `state` path, or does an undisclosed current callback require private GHSA investigation?
rationale: The protected security labels require authorized disposition, while the public report’s cited implementation surface is absent and no current-main exploit path is demonstrated.

options.title: Confirm no-action closure
options.body: Verify the device-flow implementation has no callback `state` comparison, then close the public report as targeting a nonexistent current surface.

options.title: Route to private GHSA
options.body: If a different current callback path exists, transfer the exact path and reproduction to private advisory handling before discussing remediation publicly.

options.title: Request current proof
options.body: Keep the issue open temporarily and ask for a current SHA, exact function, timing measurements, and reproduction against current main or the latest release.

recommendation.title: Confirm no-action closure
recommendation.body: Verify the device-flow implementation has no callback `state` comparison, then close the public report as targeting a nonexistent current surface.
